title: Illustration / Characters / Noses / Please don’t…
slide_intent: Place eyes on a stable area of the head so they remain visually attached as the character turns.
strategic_value: The rejected turn sequence can help Duolingo avoid facial constructions that work only from the front.
demonstration: Three crossed panels show eyes placed too high on a rounded head, followed by outlined angled views where the eyes appear to project away from the face.
practical_value: Test a head in multiple views before accepting eye placement near a curved upper edge.

content_islands.name: Rejected turn sequence
content_islands.spec: Place three red-framed, crossed examples at left, progressing from the filled front view to outlined angled views.

content_islands.name: Placement warning
content_islands.spec: Set the Please Don’t heading and single warning at right, explaining the floating-eye effect.

reference_purposes.Intent: The warning explains that eyes on a curved upper area can appear to float when the character turns.
reference_purposes.Application: The sequence demonstrates a construction problem across views.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The source warns against aligning eyes too closely with the top of the head.

ingredient.name: Eye placement on curved heads
ingredient.role: Keep eyes attached to the perceived facial plane.
ingredient.application: Avoid placing eyes too close to the curved top of the head; inspect how they behave as the character turns.
ingredient.scope: Historical official Duolingo illustration guidance from the 2024–2025 archived snapshot. This eye-placement warning appears under the source’s Noses section; preserve that original placement while classifying the construction lesson.
